keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the 220 years before Cliopatria's row: the island alone, 6 cells (about 1,517 km2) against the infobox's 1,400.68 km2 (ratio 1.08). The Rhodian Peraia page has Rhodes, Lindos, Ialysos and Kameiros 'separately possessed territory on the mainland' before 408 (the Cnidian and Trachea peninsulas) but no page opened dates or bounds the mainland holdings of 408-189, so they are left out: unverified: page budget.

188-171, 25.8 k km2 (86 cells): the island, Caria south of the Maeander (to 38.05 N) and western Lycia (to 30.5 E). The Peraia page: it 'reached its greatest extent after the Treaty of Apamea in 188 BC', with Caria and Lycia south of the Maeander under Rhodes; the Apamea page: 'most of Lycia and Caria became part of the Rhodian Peraia'. The infobox figure (1,400.68 km2) is the island only; against the gazetteer's Caria, Lycia and island together (about 38 k km2) the shape is 0.68, within the factor-of-two check.

wars.name: Roman-Seleucid War

zones.text: Caria and Lycia, the territory Rhodes was 'rewarded with'

wars.outcome: Rhodes fought alongside Rome and, by the Treaty of Apamea of 188, 'was rewarded with territory and enhanced status'; most of Lycia and Caria became the Rhodian Peraia.
wars.note: The Rhodes page gives 192-188 for the war and does not name Lycia or Caria; the Apamea and Peraia pages do.

wars.name: Third Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Rhodes sent envoys to Rome in about 169 wanting peace and citing its friendship with Perseus; the message 'was considered arrogant' and Rome's good graces for Rhodes ended. The Peraia was lost in 167 and an alliance with Rome followed in 164.
wars.note: Rhodes was not a belligerent on the Macedonian side; the war is listed for its territorial result, which the Peraia page dates to 167.

certainty.note: No frontier is given for the Peraia on any page; the island is sharp by coast.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Rhodes' (-188..-165, two identical 25.8 k km2 shapes) is the Rhodian Peraia at its greatest extent. The Wikidata id Q43048 is also on 'Domain of Rhodes' (1206-1249, the lords of Rhodes under Byzantine and then Hospitaller rule): a different state 1,400 years later, so two dossiers, not one; that row is not in this batch. The dossier is the whole Rhodian state from the synoecism of 408 (Rhodes page) to the last dated event, 39 BC (Peraia page); the end is a bridge (ledger, confidence 1) and the state in fact continued as a nominally independent ally of Rome. The Rhodes page and its sources (budget 1-2 pages) were not enough for the 167 loss, so the Treaty of Apamea, Rhodian Peraia and Third Macedonian War pages were opened as well (four pages: over budget by two, for the one border move Cliopatria misdates). Not on any page opened: the extent of the mainland holdings in 408-189, the Delian free port, the Lycian revolt, who received Caria and Lycia in 167, the date of the alliance of 164 beyond the Rhodes page, the end of Rhodian self-rule. The Peraia page's tributary 'remainder of Caria and Lycia' has an ambiguous date. Other dossiers should carry: roman-republic a vassal_start on Rhodes in 164 (alliance that 'marked a significant reduction in Rhodes's freedom of action'); seleucid-empire the loss of Caria and Lycia in 188; greek-city-states should subtract the island from 408 and the Peraia from 188. Gazetteer: the Peraia strip is a polygon because Cnidus, Kaunos and Stratonicea are not places; Caria, Lycia, Rhodes resolve.
